assessment.nobel_worthiness: The elucidation and therapeutic exploitation of GLP-1 physiology has transformed treatment of diabetes and obesity, with exceptionally broad medical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Holst and Mojsov are central to identifying the biologically active incretin, while Drucker established key physiological and translational foundations.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism and clinical benefit have been extensively confirmed across decades and large patient populations.
uncertainties: Attribution for drug development also extends to contributors not selected within the three-person limit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like-particle vaccines provided a decisive preventive strategy against common cancers and demonstrate an extraordinary public-health impact.
assessment.attribution: Frazer, Lowy, and Schiller have clear, complementary claims in the conception and development of the vaccine approach.
assessment.maturity: Long-term implementation and population evidence strongly establish prevention of HPV infection and related disease.
uncertainties: The relative division of credit among foundational and development contributions remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing converted a fatal childhood disorder into one with an effective molecular treatment, validating RNA therapeutics in medicine.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's mechanistic splicing work and Bennett's therapeutic antisense development form a coherent and limited attribution.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy and real-world use are well established, although treatment timing and access remain consequential.
uncertainties: The discovery rests on a larger chain of SMA genetics and therapeutic-development contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CAR-T therapy established a new modality in which engineered immune cells can induce durable remissions in otherwise refractory cancers.
assessment.attribution: June, Sadelain, and Rosenberg represent major and complementary clinical, engineering, and adoptive-cell-therapy contributions.
assessment.maturity: The therapeutic principle has substantial clinical validation and continuing expansion across hematologic malignancies.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed across a long developmental history, and efficacy remains uneven outside selected cancers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CFTR modulators transformed cystic fibrosis from symptomatic management toward correction of its core molecular defect.
assessment.attribution: Welsh contributed essential CFTR functional biology, and Van Goor and Negulescu made central contributions to modulator discovery and development.
assessment.maturity: Clinical benefit is robust and sustained, including for combination therapies, and the causal mechanism is clear.
uncertainties: The candidate combines foundational physiology and extensive industrial drug-development work, making the precise laureate boundary challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave experimental physiology an unprecedented means to test the causal functions of defined cells and circuits.
assessment.attribution: Deisseroth was pivotal in establishing the general method in neuroscience, while Hegemann and Nagel made essential channelrhodopsin discoveries.
assessment.maturity: The technique is widely replicated, diversified, and foundational to modern circuit neuroscience.
uncertainties: Several additional investigators have strong, intertwined claims to credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation substantially changed the treatment of Parkinson's disease and demonstrated the therapeutic power of targeted circuit modulation.
assessment.attribution: Benabid has a particularly direct and identifiable claim for the decisive clinical innovation.
assessment.maturity: Its efficacy, indications, and clinical durability have been established over many years.
uncertainties: Its framing as a therapeutic procedure rather than a biological discovery may affect comparative Nobel fit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau and alpha-synuclein as constituents of defining neurodegenerative filaments reshaped the molecular classification and study of major brain diseases.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini have closely linked and readily identifiable contributions to the central pathological protein discoveries.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been broadly confirmed and remain foundational for disease models and biomarker research.
uncertainties: The extent to which filament pathology is causally decisive rather than one component of disease remains unresolved.
Clinical disease-modifying consequences have not yet matched the explanatory importance of the discoveries.
